about.title: Inglewood Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Inglewood sits at a busy crossroads of Los Angeles County, and its streets carry a steady mix of commuters, event traffic, and neighborhood drivers. Public records for 2025 show 446 injury collisions in the city, with 635 people hurt and 7 lives lost. Prairie Avenue, Century Boulevard, Manchester Boulevard, and La Brea Avenue account for the largest share of reported crashes, and Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when reports tend to cluster. If one of those numbers now includes you, the paperwork can feel heavier than the injury itself. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent California personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives most drivers two years to file, but claims involving a city bus or other government vehicle can carry a window as short as six months. Acting early protects your options and the evidence that supports them.

whyChoose.title: Why Inglewood Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not Close the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you shared some blame, with your recovery reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no limit on non-economic damages in a standard car accident claim. Your attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Protecting Your Evidence From Day One
items.desc: Dashcam footage, photos, witness names, and medical records fade or disappear quickly. Getting connected early helps preserve them and keeps you from giving the other driver's insurer a recorded statement that could be used against you.

items.question: I was hit on Manchester Boulevard and the other driver says I was partly to blame. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Yes, you may. California uses pure comparative fault, so a claim survives even when both drivers contributed to the crash. Your compensation would simply be reduced by whatever percentage of fault is assigned to you. An attorney can gather evidence to challenge an unfair split.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster keeps calling. Should I give them a statement?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use casual remarks about how you feel or what you remember to minimize your claim. Report the crash to your own insurer as your policy requires, but keep the conversation factual and brief.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Inglewood?
items.answer: For most crashes, California allows two years from the date of injury to file a lawsuit. If a government vehicle or public agency is involved, you may need to submit a claim in as little as six months. Because the deadline depends on who was involved, it is worth getting your situation reviewed sooner rather than later.
